blocks.text: In many chemical processes the reactants are not present in the proportions of the balanced equation. Frequently a large amount of an inexpensive reactant is supplied, to ensure that the whole mass of the expensive reactant is converted to the desired product, to produce the maximum amount of product, and to increase the rate of reaction. A large quantity of oxygen makes things burn more rapidly: excess oxygen is left at the end and the other reactant, the fuel, is consumed earlier.

blocks.title: Limiting reactant
blocks.text: The reactant which is consumed earlier, and so controls the amount of product formed in a chemical reaction, is the limiting reactant or reagent. Once it is consumed the reaction stops and no additional product forms.
The amount of product that forms is limited by the reactant that is completely used, and the maximum amount of product depends on the amount of limiting reactant in the mixture.
